title: Workflows and agents: who owns the control flow?

items.stem: A workflow is a system where the program's code decides the steps. Which description makes a system an agent instead of a workflow?

options.text: It calls several different tools while handling one request
It calls the model more than once while handling one request
The model chooses the next step and decides when to stop
It answers using text taken from the machine manuals

items.stem: A makerspace assistant handles every question the same way. Step 1: code searches the manuals for the question. Step 2: the model writes an answer from the passages found. Step 3: code sends the answer to the student. The steps never change. What is this system?

options.text: A workflow, because the code fixes the steps and their order
An agent, because the model writes the final answer text
An agent, because it searches the manuals before answering
Neither, because a language model is used inside the system

items.stem: Which makerspace task is the best fit for a fixed workflow rather than an agent?

options.text: Working out why a student's 3D prints keep failing from a vague description
Answering open questions that may need several manuals and the calendar
Planning a project that needs several machines in an unknown order
Booking a machine slot using the same checks and steps every time

items.stem: The team requires that the assistant must never write a booking before it has checked the calendar. Should the booking part be a fixed workflow or an agent, and why?
Which situation is the strongest reason to choose an agent over a fixed workflow?

options.text: The steps needed are the same for every request that arrives
The next step depends on what each tool returns, so no list can be written in advance
The sponsor gave the team a very small budget for model usage
Students need an answer back in under one second

items.stem: Give one reason a fixed workflow usually costs less per request than an agent doing the same job.
